answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may submit jobs or claim rewards. A reputation score then grows only from completed work that counterparties verify, while provable fraud burns the stake and erases that identity’s record. Splitting one operator across many aliases no longer multiplies influence for free: each alias needs its own capital, and a coordinated attack risks losing it. The ocean of possible names offers no cheap ledge to stand on; an attacker must forge many funded identities and keep them honest long enough to earn trust.
